title: Commuting involutions compose to an involution
summary: Compose two reversible transformations that each undo themselves. If they commute, applying their composition twice returns the input. A concrete Lean List example reverses a Boolean list while negating each element.

source.statement: ∀ {α : Sort u} (f g : α → α), (∀ x, f (f x) = x) → (∀ x, g (g x) = x) → (∀ x, g (f x) = f (g x)) → ∀ x, (f ∘ g) ((f ∘ g) x) = x

assumptions: f and g are endofunctions on the same sort.
f is an involution: ∀ x, f (f x) = x.
g is an involution: ∀ x, g (g x) = x.
f and g commute: ∀ x, g (f x) = f (g x).

license.attribution: Ohara contributors; AI-assisted local Lean proof. Concrete Lean examples retain their Apache-2.0 attribution.

reuse: Use Lean 4.35.0. Download Pattern.lean, compile it, and import Pattern. Supply two involutions on the same sort and a proof that they commute. The retained package includes list and Boolean-pair consumers.
